reason: On the base revision REGEX_FORMAT still matches Y{1,4}, and unmatched year tokens fall through to the timezone-offset fallback, so lone Y and YYY are emitted as offsets rather than literal Y / two-digit-year-plus-Y.
After the change REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY and YY, so a lone Y is left literal and YYY is formatted as YY plus a leftover Y, which is exactly the expected output and not a UTC offset.
The base code already decodes path params that contain % via tryDecodeURIComponent, so a percent-encoded segment such as %20 is returned as the decoded character.
The PR only extracts the existing percent-decode-if-needed check into a shared helper; request parameter decoding still runs tryDecodeURIComponent, so %20 is still returned as a space.
Before the fix reschedule writes the new score to Redis but never updates @score, so the same in-memory handle still reports the pre-reschedule time.
The head revision sets @score = at.to_f after zincrby, so entry.score and entry.at on the same object immediately match the new reschedule time.
The change only trims whitespace in Range header parsing and does not touch Content-Type parsing, which already reads type, subtype, and charset from a header such as text/plain; charset=UTF-8.
The Range-header trim is unrelated to Content-Type; parsing text/plain; charset=UTF-8 and reading back charset=UTF-8 is unchanged and still holds.
The diff only sanitizes download/signature error messages in ComposerRepository and does not alter zip archiving, so source file mtimes should still be stored and restored from the archive.
Re-archiving is likewise unaffected by the logging-only change, so repeated zip extracts should keep the same source-matching modification times rather than collapsing to 1980-01-01.
CredentialCache prefix matching is unrelated to System.Text.Json; asynchronous DeserializeAsync of a list with a nullable parent property is not touched by this diff and should still complete.
The CredentialCache path-comparison change cannot make async JSON deserialization diverge from the synchronous path, so both calls should still return equivalent object graphs.
The PR only fixes FETCH FIRST on an empty WITH HOLD cursor and does not change INET operators, so <<= ANY should still parse and return true for an address inside the subnet.
The cursor FETCH change is unrelated to INET >>= ANY; the statement should still execute and return true because 10.0.0.0/8 contains 10.1.2.3.
On the base revision every NO_PROXY entry is turned into all://*<hostname>, so ::1 becomes an invalid URL pattern and client construction errors instead of treating it as an IPv6 bypass host.
After the fix IPv6 NO_PROXY values are mounted as all://[::1], so constructing a client with NO_PROXY=::1 no longer blows up in URL parsing.

The prior flags validation compiled the pattern then compared the full reconstructed flag set, which rejects DOTALL (and compiled patterns carrying it), so the match is raised rather than honouring dot-matches-newline.
The head revision stops requiring full flag-set equality and only pre-compiles extra flags such as DOTALL, so both flags= and a compiled DOTALL pattern match 'a\nc' and not 'ac'.

Before the fix, freeze/prepare_steps does not refresh prev_task/prev_res after a mid-chain group, so a chain with two sequential groups serializes an incomplete result tree and reconstruction drops child results.
The added prev_task/prev_res update after a group keeps later groups linked correctly, so the reconstructed tree still has a child result for each of the four grouped tasks.
The reported bug is only when -- is the first argument; here value1 value2 precede --, so the first positional still stops at the terminator and the later positional still receives --check.
The new terminator check prefers the current positional's value_terminator over trailing-values mode, which preserves the mid-stream -- handoff of --check to the second positional.
On the base revision a post-startup OSC 11 response calls nvim_set_option_value('background'), which updates the option and fires OptionSet and the usual ColorScheme side effects the test expects.
The head revision sets background with :noautocmd specifically to suppress OptionSet (and other autocommands) on late OSC 11, so the registered OptionSet and ColorScheme handlers do not fire.

Reordering the @derive attribute read only affects compile-time Inspect coupling and does not change changeset cast/validate_required, so an omitted required field is still invalid with a blank error.
The same derive-read reorder is still unrelated to required-field validation, so the changeset remains invalid with a can't-be-blank error after the PR.
